title: A spring, a rough patch and a ramp

stimulus.title: A spring, a rough patch and a ramp
stimulus.html: A block of mass m is held against a spring of spring constant k, compressing it by x, at point P, and released. The block leaves the spring, slides across a rough patch of length D where the coefficient of kinetic friction is μ, and then slides up a frictionless curved ramp. It momentarily stops at point R, a height H above the floor. The rest of the floor is frictionless. Air resistance is negligible.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Take the block, the spring, Earth and the floor (including the rough patch) as the system. On the bar charts, draw shaded bars showing the kinetic energy K, elastic potential energy U_s, gravitational potential energy U_g and thermal energy E_th of the system when the block is at P and when it is at R. Take U_g = 0 and E_th = 0 at P. Bars should be drawn to the same scale.

rubric.point: At P: only a nonzero U_s bar (K, U_g and E_th are zero).
accept: P chart shows U_s alone
block at rest so no K at P

rubric.point: At R: K and U_s are zero; U_g and E_th are both nonzero.
accept: R chart has U_g and E_th only
block momentarily at rest at R

rubric.point: The U_g and E_th bars at R add up to the U_s bar at P.
accept: total bar height is the same at P and R
no energy crosses the system boundary

parts.sample: At P: a U_s bar of, say, 5 units; K, U_g and E_th zero. At R: K = 0 and U_s = 0 (the block is at rest and has left the spring); U_g = 3 units and E_th = 2 units. The totals match (5 units), because the system is closed: no external force does work on it.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Derive an expression for H in terms of m, k, x, μ, D and physical constants, as appropriate. Your equation should be consistent with your bar charts in part (a).

rubric.point: Writes an energy equation with one term for each nonzero bar: ½kx² = mgH + E_th.
accept: U_s at P = U_g at R + thermal energy
conservation of energy for the closed system

rubric.point: Uses E_th = μmgD for the energy dissipated by kinetic friction on the patch.
accept: work done by friction is −μmgD
friction force μmg over distance D
H = (½kx² − μmgD)/(mg)
H = kx²/(2mg) − μD

parts.sample: The system is closed, so its energy is constant: U_s(P) = U_g(R) + E_th, i.e. ½kx² = mgH + μmgD (on the patch the normal force is mg, so friction is μmg acting over D). So H = kx²/(2mg) − μD.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: On the axes, sketch a graph of the kinetic energy of the block as a function of its horizontal position, from P to R. Mark where the block leaves the spring and where the rough patch begins and ends.

rubric.point: K starts at zero at P and increases until the block leaves the spring (relaxed length), then is constant on the frictionless floor.
accept: rises from 0, then horizontal
maximum K where the spring is relaxed

rubric.point: K decreases linearly (constant negative slope) across the rough patch, then is constant again until the ramp.
accept: straight-line drop across the patch
slope −μmg on the patch

rubric.point: K decreases to zero at R.
accept: K reaches zero at the highest point
ends on the position axis at R

parts.sample: Starting at 0 at P, K rises along a curve that flattens out (the spring's push weakens) to its maximum, ½kx², where the block leaves the spring. It is flat until the patch, falls in a straight line across the patch (friction is a constant μmg, so K drops by μmg per meter), is flat again until the ramp, and then falls to zero at R.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Explain how your bar charts, your equation in part (b) and your graph in part (c) are consistent with one another. Refer to a specific feature of each.

rubric.point: Links the U_s bar at P to the ½kx² term and to the maximum K on the graph (where the block leaves the spring).
accept: the stored spring energy becomes the peak kinetic energy
U_s bar ↔ ½kx² ↔ highest point of the graph

rubric.point: Links the E_th bar to the μmgD term and to the straight-line drop in K across the rough patch, whose size is μmgD.
accept: thermal energy bar equals the K lost on the patch
E_th ↔ μmgD ↔ linear decrease

rubric.point: Links the U_g bar at R to the mgH term and to K falling to zero at R.
accept: the remaining kinetic energy becomes U_g on the ramp
U_g bar ↔ mgH ↔ K = 0 at R

parts.sample: The U_s bar at P is the ½kx² term, and it is also the peak of the K graph, reached as the block leaves the spring. The E_th bar is the μmgD term, and it equals the height of the straight-line drop in K across the patch. The U_g bar at R is the mgH term: the kinetic energy left after the patch falls to zero on the ramp as it becomes U_g. The bars add to the same total, the equation balances, and the graph starts and ends at K = 0.

x.label: Horizontal position of the block, from P to R

drawSpec.label: Energy bar charts for the block-spring-Earth-floor system at P and at R
